key_headlines.title: Government Launches Startup Initiative to Create 10 'Startup Cities' by 2030
key_headlines.summary: The South Korean government announced plans to designate 10 startup cities, starting with four locations hosting science and technology institutes, and invest 2 trillion won in specialized funds by 2030 to foster youth employment and regional development.

key_headlines.title: Q1 GDP Growth Surprises at 1.7%, Double Government's 0.9% Forecast
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's first-quarter GDP growth came in at 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, significantly exceeding expectations and prompting analysts to raise full-year growth forecasts to potentially 2.4-3%.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Reaches Record Highs Near 6,500 as KOSDAQ Settles at 1,200 Level
key_headlines.summary: South Korean stock indices hit historic highs with the KOSPI approaching 6,500 and KOSDAQ stabilizing around 1,200, driven by strong semiconductor performance and positive economic data.

key_headlines.title: Yellow Envelope Law Implementation Impacts Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Across Industries
key_headlines.summary: One month after the Yellow Envelope Law amendment to labor laws took effect, labor disputes between unions at major companies and their subcontractors have spread nationwide, with small businesses in steel, shipbuilding, and automotive sectors facing increasing damage.

key_headlines.title: U.S. Department of Justice Halts Investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Powell
key_headlines.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice discontinued its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, clearing the way for confirmation of his successor Bessent and marking a shift in Trump administration pressure tactics.

sections.Hot Economy News: The South Korean government is launching an ambitious 'startup boom' initiative targeting job creation and regional economic development through 10 strategically designated startup cities by 2030. The government plans to invest 2 trillion won in specialized funds and designate initial cities in Daejeon, Daegu, Gwangju, and Ulsan where science and technology institutes are located, with six additional cities added by next year. This policy shift aims to transform youth employment from job-seeking to job-creation while simultaneously revitalizing local economies. The government is also expanding its 'Everyone's Startup' program with an additional 2 billion won in supplementary budget allocation and fostering 17 glocal commercial districts.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's first-quarter GDP growth surprised positively at 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, nearly double the Bank of Korea's February forecast of 0.9%, the strongest performance in five years and eight months since Q3 2020. This robust growth has prompted financial institutions and analysts to upwardly revise full-year 2026 growth forecasts, with some predicting Korea could achieve 3% growth. However, underlying inflation pressures from war-related global commodity price increases have prompted concerns about future monetary policy, with debate ongoing whether the central bank will maintain its accommodative stance or pursue rate hikes. Meanwhile, the Philippines' central bank raised its benchmark rate despite economic slowdown concerns, responding to persistent inflation pressures from geopolitical disruptions affecting energy and fertilizer prices.
sections.Financial Markets: South Korean stock indices have reached historic highs with the KOSPI approaching 6,500 and the KOSDAQ settling around 1,200 for the first time in 25 years, driven by strong semiconductor performance and positive macroeconomic data. However, volatility remains elevated in the KOSPI 6,000 era, prompting renewed interest in index-linked insurance products that offer principal guarantees alongside equity upside potential. The won-to-dollar exchange rate has appreciated for the fourth consecutive day amid U.S.-Iran tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, adding currency volatility to market dynamics. Global central bank decisions from the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan scheduled for the week ahead are expected to significantly influence market direction, with consensus expectations pointing toward policy hold decisions.
sections.Industry & Technology: A month after the Yellow Envelope Law took effect on March 10, labor disputes have escalated rapidly, with 1,077 unit unions targeting 393 small and medium-sized enterprises, creating a cascading impact through supply chains in steel, shipbuilding, and automotive sectors. South Korea and Vietnam reinforced their science and technology cooperation through a joint innovation forum, agreeing to strengthen collaboration in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, secondary batteries, biotechnology, energy, and mineral resources. The domestic stock market is showing clear sectional concentration with power equipment, semiconductor, and shipbuilding stocks recording new highs and capturing investor attention. The government is advancing plans to expand AI data centers and semiconductor clusters, though projecting maximum power demand could reach 131.8-138.2GW by 2040, creating infrastructure challenges and local resistance to power transmission line construction.
sections.Real Estate: South Korean real estate markets continue to face structural challenges, with reports indicating extreme price levels in international markets like Hong Kong where small two-bedroom apartments command 500-700 million won. Suspicious family property transactions involving price manipulation, illegal gifting, and loan diversion are being flagged, with 99 cases of business loan misuse for residential purchases confirmed in Seoul and metropolitan areas. The strong demand for small apartments in Gangnam through lottery-style apartment allocations has reignited debate over point-based allocation systems, with some first-time homebuyers abandoning apartment aspirations in favor of villa investments in redevelopment areas. Former Land Minister Byun Chang-heum warned that private redevelopment projects are driving up overall housing prices by supplying ultra-luxury apartments at 200 million won per pyeong in Seoul's core areas, and advocated for inclusive housing policies based on mid-rise, high-density development.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Department of Justice has discontinued its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, widely interpreted as a strategic shift in the Trump administration's approach to the central bank, potentially accelerating confirmation of successor nominee Bessent. Multiple analysts view the investigation discontinuation as political pressure tactics, as Bessent has indicated at confirmation hearings that central banks must maintain independence while acknowledging presidential preferences for rate cuts. The upcoming week features critical central bank decisions from the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of Japan, with consensus expectations pointing toward policy holds, though market implications remain uncertain. Geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran continue to escalate with additional sanctions on 40 shipping companies in Iran's shadow fleet, while Iran has reportedly added mines to the Strait of Hormuz, threatening critical global energy transit routes.
sections.AI & Economy: Survey results from AI company Anthropic indicate a paradox where increased generative AI adoption correlates with higher job displacement anxiety, despite documented productivity improvements, with 81,000 users surveyed expressing growing concerns about AI replacing their work. Policy discussions highlight the need to overhaul distribution regulations inherited from previous frameworks and redesign policies aligned with the AI era, as existing restrictions on large retailers and SSM franchises fail to protect traditional markets while creating consumer inconvenience and business closures. Japan's approach to AI integration with 125 million people maintains traditional employment practices, providing stable salaries to large workforces to sustain domestic consumption rather than pursuing maximum efficiency. Experts emphasize the necessity for proactive infrastructure and education safety nets to prevent a small group from monopolizing AI-driven data advantages and to address accelerating labor market disruptions.
sections.Others: Fragile U.S.-Iran negotiations continue amid military posturing, with the Trump administration deploying a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East while Iran responds with additional mine installations in the Strait of Hormuz, creating economic risks through potential energy market disruption. The U.S. and EU have agreed to explore common pricing floors for critical minerals to reduce dependence on Chinese supplies, signaling a multilateral coordination approach to mineral security with Japan also participating in discussions. Contrarian investor Michael Burry, previously skeptical of AI bubble valuations, has reversed course and begun purchasing major software and cloud computing stocks including Microsoft and Adobe, repositioning his portfolio amid AI integration pressures. The Korean education sector has mobilized unified resistance to government suggestions of restructuring local education finance transfers, with 17 provincial education superintendent associations preparing formal statements opposing the proposed reforms.
